MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER / SKYDIO

//Skydio

Tech: Autonomous flight

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give responders a live aerial view across long distances, where time counts more than the ground they must cover.

Why: With a 30-mile flight radius, one MegaDock can put nearly 3,000 square miles within reach of a single launch location.

Traction: F10 is set to deploy to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio was founded in 2014. F10 Lightrunner is the company's first fixed-wing aircraft. Its robotic takeoff and landing system uses a suction-based gripper to launch and catch the aircraft. Skydio says each MegaDock can house up to five F10s, letting one team run several missions at once.

Source: Skydio, September 24, 2026

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE

//L3Harris

Tech: Counter-drone weapons

Platform: Self-contained weapons system

Goal: Defeat drones and remotely piloted platforms across domains with reconnaissance and precision strike.

Why: The U.S. Navy selected the system for littoral counter-unmanned systems defense, and L3Harris says it is being engineered for new mission needs and maritime conditions.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems, per L3Harris. L3Harris is also delivering VAMPIRE systems to the U.S. Army.

L3Harris said it unveiled Wraith Shield software earlier in 2026. It provides a radio-as-a-sensor capability against small drones and can be paired with VAMPIRE and Drone Guardian systems for layered defense. Drone Guardian is described by the company as an operationally proven counter-UAS system.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, in the Gulf of America.

Why: The vessels are solar powered and can stay on station for multiple months.

Traction: Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026 in support of federal border security efforts, and a Lightfish fleet has now been deployed to the Gulf of America, per Seasats.

Seasats announced that a Lightfish fleet has been deployed for U.S. maritime border security. The vessels were launched from the Texas coast and extend an autonomous maritime surveillance program Seasats already runs for the Homeland Defense office within the Assistant Secretary of War portfolio.

Each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and weighs about 340 pounds, and two people can launch and recover one from a boat ramp or a pickup truck bed. Earlier missions have fitted its cameras, signals gear and sonar into a swappable equipment bay.

The Gulf deployment follows Seasats' earlier support of Operation River Wall on the southern border. Mike Flanigan, CEO of Seasats, has said the company has over $100 million in U.S. government contracts.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, 2026-10-02

Image: prnewswire.com (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // EAGLEEYE / ANDURIL

//Anduril Industries

Tech: AI-enhanced digital vision

Platform: Warfighter augment

Goal: Give warfighters threat detection, Blue Force tracking and battlefield awareness in one wearable system.

Why: Operators keep their eyes up and on the move while tasking unmanned vehicles, calling for fires and controlling robotic teammates.

Traction: Described on Anduril's EagleEye product page as a family of warfighter augments powered by Lattice. The page does not give a fielding or test status.

EagleEye overlays AI-enhanced digital vision, Blue Force tracking and 6DOF spatial awareness onto the real world. Its sensing mix spans RF detection, rearview cameras, non-emissive lasers, biometric and environmental monitoring, and instant battlefield alerts. A 1km threat detection capability uses optical zoom EO and LWIR cameras, and an 8 microphone array detects and localizes gunshots and drones.

The display runs at a 90 Hz refresh with a 200° HFOV x 90° VFOV field of view. The ballistic shell is rated NIJ IIIA Level. A high-resolution collaborative 3D sand table supports mission command, remote mission planning sessions and mission rehearsals.

Anduril describes Lattice as the software platform that powers its software-defined weapons and connects with third-party and government-owned capabilities. Anduril Industries, Inc. is an American defense technology company focused on advanced autonomous systems, according to the company's page.

Source: Anduril Industries, date not stated on page

Image: Anduril (courtesy)
